'''''Pistacia atlantica''''' is a species of [[Pistacia|pistachio tree]] known by the [[English language|English]] common names '''Mt. Atlas mastic tree''', '''Mount Atlas pistachio''', '''Atlantic pistachio''', '''wild pistachio''', '''turpentine tree'''<ref>{{Catalogue of Life |id=4J9TB |title=''Pistacia atlantica'' Desf. |option=taxon |access-date=5 May 2026}}</ref> and '''Atlantic terebinth'''.
''P. atlantica'' has three subspecies or varieties which have been described as ''atlantica'', ''cabulica,'' and ''mutica''. According to [[molecular phylogenetic]] studies, ''P. atlantica'' subsp. ''kurdica'' is actually a separate species, ''[[Pistacia eurycarpa]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kafkas |first1=S. |last2=Perl-Treves |first2=R. |date=2001-05-01 |title=Morphological and molecular phylogeny of ''Pistacia'' species in Turkey |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/225673348 |journal=Theoretical and Applied Genetics |language=en |volume=102 |issue=6 |pages=908–915 |doi=10.1007/s001220000526 |s2cid=2967504 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kafkas |first=S. |date=2006-11-01 |title=Phylogenetic analysis of the genus ''Pistacia'' by AFLP markers |journal=Plant Systematics and Evolution |language=en |volume=262 |issue=1 |pages=113–124 |doi=10.1007/s00606-006-0460-7 |s2cid=570340 |jstor=23655617|bibcode=2006PSyEv.262..113K }}</ref>

==Names==
In Kurdish it is called Qazwan, Wanataq and ''bana''.<ref name="pourreza">{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/s10722-017-0522-4 | title=Traditional uses of Kurdish medicinal plant ''Pistacia atlantica'' subsp. ''kurdica'' Zohary in Ranya, Southern Kurdistan | date=2017 | last1=Ahmed | first1=Hiwa M. | journal=Genetic Resources and Crop Evolution | volume=64 | issue=6 | pages=1473–1484 | bibcode=2017GRCEv..64.1473A | s2cid=254504017 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317003852}}</ref> In [[Berber languages|Tamazight]], it is known as Tijjeɣt. In the Canary Islands it is known as Almacigo, and in Arabic it is called {{lang|ar|بطم}} (''buṭm'' or ''buṭum''). In southern [[Iran]], in [[Bandar-Abbas]] in [[Hormozgān Province]], it is called  ''kasoudang'' and in [[Bushehr]] it is called  ''kolkhong''. In [[Turkey]] it is commonly known as  ''melengiç''. In Kurdish the tree is called darwan or daraban, and the seed is called qezwan or jajig (قەزوان_جاجگ). In Pashto it is called Shanna. And in Birhavi/Balochi it is called Gowan.{{cn|date=June 2023}} In Hebrew it is called Elah Atlantit.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MAY: Atlantic Pistacia - Elah Atlantit-אלה אטלנטית |url=https://www.kkl-jnf.org/forestry-and-ecology/tress-in-kkl-jnf-forests/israel-tree-of-the-month/may-atlantic-pistacia/}}</ref> In Malta, it is known as Deru tal-Atlantiku, Pistaċċa bagħla.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pistacia atlantica   (Mount Atlas Pistachio) |url=https://www.maltawildplants.com/ANCR/Pistacia_atlantica.php}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Pistacia atlantica, Elah Valley, June 2015.jpg|thumb|left|''Pistacia atlantica'' in [[Elah valley]]]]
''Pistacia atlantica'' is a [[deciduous]] tree growing up to {{convert|7|m|abbr=on}} tall with branches spreading and growing erect to form a dense crown. The trunk is stout and covered in fissured bark. Old trees may have trunks measuring {{convert|2|m|abbr=on}} in diameter; it may take 200 years for a tree to reach {{convert|1|m|abbr=on}} wide.<ref name=pourreza/> The leaves are pinnate, each with seven to 9 lance-shaped leaflets.

The leaves and branches often have [[gall]]s when the tree is infested with gall-producing species of [[aphid]]s, including ''[[Pemphigus utricularis]]'',<ref name=fao/> ''[[Slavum wertheimae]]'', and ''[[Forda riccobonii]]''.<ref name=martinez>{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/s11829-008-9042-7 | title=Impact of a gall-inducing aphid on ''Pistacia atlantica'' Desf. trees | date=2008 | last1=Martinez | first1=J.-J. I. | journal=Arthropod-Plant Interactions | volume=2 | issue=3 | pages=147–151 | bibcode=2008APInt...2..147M | s2cid=43684928 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/248134588}}</ref>

The tree is [[dioecious]] with male and female trees producing different types of flowers. Both types are small and greenish and fall away quickly. [[Monoecious]] and [[hermaphrodite]] trees have been seen, but are unusual.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.22069/IJPP.2012.656 | date=2009 | volume=3 | issue=3 | last1=İsfendiyaroğlu | first1=M. | last2=Özeker | first2=E. | title=Inflorescence features of a new exceptional monoecious ''Pistacia atlantica'' Desf. (Anacardiaceae) population in the Barbaros Plain of İzmir/Turkey | journal=International Journal of Plant Production|doi-access=free|url=http://www.gau.ac.ir/Jm/Programs/JurnalMgr/VolumArticle/EN_135_3.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722015053/http://www.gau.ac.ir/Jm/Programs/JurnalMgr/VolumArticle/EN_135_3.pdf | archive-date=2011-07-22 }}</ref> The oblong, fleshy, oily fruit borne by the female tree is {{convert|6|to|8|mm|abbr=on}} long and pink in color, ripening to blue. The tree grows slowly, and can reach 1000 years old. It has broken bark with ashen gray color. Older branches have the same design, fractured and ash color, which gives the tree a grizzled look. The leaves are oval, almost sessile, shining above, and dark green, with seven to 9 leaflets, imparipinnate with [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]s a little winged, flowers in racemes lax, the male and female on different trees.{{cn|date=June 2023}}

<ref>{{Cite web |title=Variegated Pistacia atlantica in the Crimea |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381113509_Variegated_Pistacia_atlantica_in_the_Crimea}}</ref>The flowers are [[unisexual]], small, discreet green, thick as pea fruit, then changing to reddish blue.<ref>{{cite book|last=Ozenda|first=P.|title=Flore et Végétation du Sahara|publisher=París:CNRS|year=1991|isbn=2-271-06230-6}}</ref>
In colder areas the leaves in May check and fall in November. Though dioecious, in some communities males dominate the female specimens in number. It grows in [[oak]] woodlands and oak [[sclerophyll]]us. The fruits ripen from July to October, starting to bear fruit at the age of eight to 10 years, with abundant fruit after two to three years.{{cn|date=June 2023}}

==Distribution==
It is native to a section of [[Eurasia]] from [[North Africa]] to the [[Iranian Plateau]], where it was once common.<ref name=fao>[https://web.archive.org/web/20150525010128/http://www.fao.org/ag/agp/AGPC/doc/gbase/new_species/pistatl.htm ''Pistacia atlantica'' Desf.] FAO Fact Sheet</ref> Because other trees were rare, it was the only good source of [[wood]] and was [[Overexploitation|overharvested]], reducing its current distribution.<ref name=fao/> It is a common tree in mountain forests in Iran,<ref name=fao/> and it is "characteristic" of the landscape in parts of [[Algeria]] outside the [[Sahara]].<ref name=yousfi>{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/s11746-002-0601-8 | title=Fatty acids and sterols of ''Pistacia atlantica'' fruit oil | date=2002 | last1=Yousfi | first1=M. | last2=Nedjmi | first2=B. | last3=Bellal | first3=R. | last4=Ben Bertal | first4=D. | last5=Palla | first5=G. | journal=Journal of the American Oil Chemists' Society | volume=79 | issue=10 | pages=1049–1050 | s2cid=94601571 |url=http://lib3.dss.go.th/fulltext/Journal/J.AOCS/J.AOCS/2002/no.10/v.79n10p1049-1050.pdf|display-authors=1}}</ref>

The ''almacigo'' is a tree that extends from the North Africa and found in thermophilous forests, up to 600 m altitude. It is one of the few deciduous species native to the Canary archipelago.
It is native of Eurasia, the [[Iran|Iranian Plateau]], to northern Africa.<ref Name=fao/>
<!-- reword, Also in the northern [[Sahara]], in the region of the [[Sahara Desert|dayas]] at the foot of [[Atlas (mountains)|Atlas]] Moroccan and Algerian Sahara, is rare in the solid [[Hoggar]]. Northwest Morocco and Canary Islands, where it is protected by the "Annex II of the Order of the regional legislation Flora of the Canary Islands." Is found in all the Canary Islands under La Palma and El Hierro. In Gran Canaria form monospecific thickets in several western cliffs of the island, where it tends to hold the funds and the wetter areas, among Agaete and San Nicolas de Tolentino.-->Azerbaijan (Soltanbud forest)

In the Crimea, where it is a protected species, it is the only native species of the genus ''Pistacia.''<ref>{{Cite web |title=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381113509_Variegated_Pistacia_atlantica_in_the_Crimea |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381113509_Variegated_Pistacia_atlantica_in_the_Crimea}}</ref>

==Uses==
[[File:Pistacia atlantica, in sunlight.jpg|thumb|right|''Pistacia atlantica'' in sunlight]]
There are many uses for this plant. This wild pistachio is the most economically important tree in many parts of the Kurdish regions, including the [[Zagros Mountains]], where it is [[Forest management|managed]] as a valuable forest tree.<ref name=pourreza/> The [[resin]] and fruit oil were historically used for a variety of [[herbalism|medicinal purposes]].<ref name=fao/> The resin, known in Iran as ''saqez'', is still an important commodity.<ref name=pourreza/>

Another important use is to combat [[soil erosion]]. It strengthens the soil, and is used for reforestation of arid and steep slopes and against [[landslide]]s. It is stronger than ''[[Pistacia terebinthus]]'', where it is used as rootstock in Ukraine and the United States for growing ''[[Pistacia vera]]'', but resists frost better than ''P. terebinthus''.{{cn|date=June 2023}}

The resin is used to manufacture alcohol and [[lacquer]]. Its [[essential oil]]s are used in perfume industry. The leaves are rich in [[tannin]]s, up to 20% in the galls caused by an [[aphid]] parasite, used as the raw material for [[Tanning (leather)|tanning]] in the leather industry. The sap is dried and used as incense, and its smoke releases a pleasant smell to the local environment for celebrations and religious ceremonies, as "[[incense]]".

===Food===
The pistachio fruits are a food source in the area, but the more commonly cultivated pistachio tree ''P. vera'' is more valuable for food production.<ref name=pourreza/> The seeds, like pistachio, are edible [[oil seed]]s, like nuts, and contain up to 60% fat. Candy made with ''P. atlantica'' in Turkish are called ''tsukpi pistachio''. Sometimes, the immature fruit is harvested and eaten with [[sour milk]]. The plant contains a [[resin]], used as chewing gum in Kevan, Turkey, where it is called ''kevove'' rubber tree.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jungle Dragon: Persian turpentine tree |url=https://www.jungledragon.com/specie/22502/persian_turpentine_tree.html}}</ref>

The resin of the tree is called Cyprus turpentine or Cyprus balsam and used to make chewing gum in [[Cyprus]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Lardos |first1=Andreas |last2=Prieto-Garcia |first2=José |last3=Heinrich |first3=Michael |date=2011 |title=Resins and Gums in Historical Iatrosophia Texts from Cyprus – A Botanical and Medico-pharmacological Approach |journal=Frontiers in Pharmacology |volume=2 |page=32 |doi=10.3389/fphar.2011.00032 |pmc=3130153 |pmid=21772820 |doi-access=free}}</ref> in the area of [[Paphos]]. It is known as "Paphos Gum," or "Paphitiki Pissa" (Παφίτικη Πίσσα, Πίσσα Παφίτικη) in [[Cypriot Greek]].<ref>"Pafitiki Pissa – Pafos Gum." Cyprus Highlights. https://www.cyprushighlights.com/en/pafitiki-pissa-pafos-gum/, retrieved 2024-07-30.</ref> It has been reported to have significant [[antimicrobial]] and [[antifungal]] activity. Twenty-six compounds in [[hexane]] extract were identified. The major compounds were [[α-pinene]] 57.06%, [[β-pinene]] 9.83%, trans-[[pinocarveol]] 2.95%, trans-[[Verbenol]] 3.97%, α-Phellandren-8-ol 3.81%.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.acgpubs.org/doc/2018080513584611_RNP_0811_55.pdf | hdl=2268/16020 | title=Chemical Composition of the Essential Oil of ''Pistacia lentiscus'' L. From Eastern Morocco | journal=Records of Natural Products | date=2009 | volume=3 | issue=2 | last1=Amhamdi | first1=Hassan | last2=Aounti | first2=Fatima | last3=Wathelet | first3=Jean-Paul | last4=Elbachiri | first4=Ali |pages=90–95|issn=1307-6167}}</ref>

It is used in a food in [[Fars province]] in [[Iran]], named "OuBanneh" (اوبنه).

The raw fruits of the wild pistachio are not favored as food and are said to taste like [[turpentine]].<ref name=PFAF>{{Cite web |title=Pistacia atlantica |url=https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Pistacia+atlantica |access-date=2023-08-12 |website=PFAF Plant Database}}</ref> They are about 45% oil.<ref name=yousfi/>

The Jewish source The Mishnah, compiled in 200 CE in Tzippori and Beit Shearim, Israel, mentions that the roots of the tree were also consumed, but only after they were pickled in salt or vinegar.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Encyclopedia.com Terebinth |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/plants-and-animals/plants/plants/terebinth}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Cambridge Mishnah |url=https://www.50treasures.divinity.cam.ac.uk/treasure/the-cambridge-mishnah/}}</ref>

===Cultivation===
''Pistacia atlantica'' is planted as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental]] [[shade tree|shadebearing]] and [[Xeriscaping|drought-tolerant]] landscape tree in [[garden]]s and [[park]]s.<ref>University of Arizona CE. [https://web.archive.org/web/20020918083109/http://ag.arizona.edu/pima/gardening/aridplants/Pistacia_atlantica.html ''Pistacia atlantica'']</ref> In [[California]] it is imported to use as [[rootstock]] for cultivated pistachio trees (''Pistacia vera'').<ref name=jeps>[http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?315,318,319 Jepson Manual Treatment]</ref> Both [[introduced species|introductions]] have led to its escape and current status as an occasional [[invasive species]] in California.<ref>LA & San Gabriel River Council. [http://weedwatch.lasgrwc.org/docs/matrix/Pistacia_atlantica_03172007.pdf ''Pistacia atlantica''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110902052817/http://weedwatch.lasgrwc.org/docs/matrix/Pistacia_atlantica_03172007.pdf |date=2011-09-02 }}</ref>

=== References in Ancient Texts ===
Both the Book of Genesis and Chronicles refer to the tree, but it is mentioned under the general Hebrew term ''Elah,'' so it is difficult to know if the reference is to a terebinth or Pistacia atlantica.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MAY: Atlantic Pistacia - Elah Atlantit-אלה אטלנטית |url=https://kkl-jnf.org/forestry-and-ecology/tress-in-kkl-jnf-forests/israel-tree-of-the-month/may-atlantic-pistacia/}}</ref> It is also referred to in the Mishnah, in regard to its shoots.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TEREBINTH |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/plants-and-animals/plants/plants/terebinth}}</ref>
